title: orion init: show an agent-autonomy notice and ask to continue, with --yes to skip
story: orion init used to install straight away. Now it first says that orion's agents claim issues, file tickets and merge their own pull requests on green, and asks to continue. --yes skips the question, and a shell with no terminal must pass it, the same rule uninstall follows.

checks.criterion: The notice and question appear on an interactive init.
checks.steps: In a terminal, make an empty folder, then run bash orion.sh init --project <folder> --no-statusline --update-mode ask and answer n.
checks.expected: The notice listing that agents claim issues, file tickets and merge their own pull requests, then 'Install orion in <folder> on these terms? [y/N]', then 'aborted', and the folder is still empty.

checks.steps: Run the same command with --yes on a new empty folder.
checks.expected: The notice and no question; .claude/orion/VERSION and CLAUDE.md exist.

checks.criterion: With no terminal and no --yes, init refuses.
checks.steps: Run the first command with </dev/null added and its output captured to a file.
checks.expected: 'refusing to init without --yes in a non-interactive shell', exit code 1, and nothing written.
